note: FULL FRESH DEPLOYMENT of the native-mode (v3.1) contract set. Nothing was upgraded in place: the v1 URP at 0x79F0...2c1D was NOT proxied and cannot be upgraded, so this generation deploys a new upgradeable URP behind a TransparentUpgradeableProxy. Every address below is new. The v1 book is retained, superseded, and universal-only.

factoryProxy.note: PERMANENT, user-facing. This is the address the SDK and every integration uses. It does not change across factory-logic upgrades. Live-checked: deployWallet succeeded and the clone reports isWallet == true.

factoryLogic.note: UUPS implementation behind factoryProxy. Never addressed directly. Source unchanged from v1; redeployed because it must be initialised with the new wallet implementation.

walletImplementation.note: Clone template. Every wallet is a minimal clone of this with 40 bytes of immutable args (owner 0-19, factory 20-39). NEW IN v3.1: grantMandate takes a MandateType, native mandates carry 1..8 actions, and _gateAndDispatch refuses the wallet and the engine as dispatch targets. Its `urp` arg is the PROXY, so wallets keep working across URP upgrades. Grew 10,515 -> 11,626 B.

urp.note: PERMANENT, and the address every wallet pins as its canonical policy. THIS IS THE PROXY - always address URP here, never at the implementation. Initialised atomically in its constructor, so no front-run window ever existed.

urpImplementation.note: The security boundary, and the only novel contract. Sole action policy on every mandate, in BOTH modes; stripping it fails closed. Storage layout is frozen and append-only: slots 0-2 anchors, 3 $configs, 4 $credited, 5 $mode (NEW), 6 $native (NEW), 7..49 __gap[43]. Read `version()` through the proxy to confirm which implementation is live.

urpProxyAdmin.verificationBlocker: Created by an INNER CREATE from the TransparentUpgradeableProxy constructor. This Blockscout instance does not index internally-created contracts, so it reports `is_contract: false` and refuses verification with 'Address is not a smart-contract'. The chain disagrees: eth_getCode returns 926 bytes and `owner()` answers correctly. Explorer-indexer limitation, not a deployment defect.
urpProxyAdmin.note: KEEP THIS ADDRESS - no URP upgrade is possible without it. TUP creates it internally and returns it nowhere; it was read from the ERC-1967 admin slot (0xb531...6103) of the URP proxy and re-read live to confirm. Owner is the deployer EOA for testnet; production should hold this in a multisig.

sessionValidator.note: Stateless. Source UNCHANGED from v1. Its address is an input to every permission id, so mandates granted against the v1 validator do not carry over to this generation - which is expected, since this is a fresh deployment and no v1 state is preserved.

sessionEngine.note: Vendored fork 7dc20e4, adopted unmodified. Installed as each wallet's only validator module. Runtime margin is 1,995 B - the tightest in the set, which is why optimizer_runs is pinned at 833.

adminState.note: Admin is the deployer EOA for testnet. TWO distinct upgrade authorities now exist: the factory's DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE (UUPS upgrade of factory logic - the only action that can strand counterfactually funded addresses) and the URP ProxyAdmin owner (can replace every gate in the policy). A production deployment should hold both in a multisig, and they should not be the same key.

smokeTest.note: A REAL wallet through the REAL factory, not a simulation. Proves the whole stack is wired: registry, clone immutable args, URP pin, and the engine installed as the sole validator module.
